search_strategy: Grep-first over three bulk exports: it curled/scripted the full Mattermost history to /tmp/chat.txt.n and grepped for retry-vocabulary regexes ('retry_policy|RetryPolicy|classify_failure|FailureClass|failure class|thro...') in single wide passes (e.g. L1370-1400 hits 8 different remarks at once), which is efficient but returns only the matching line plus whatever narrow -A/-B context the grep call asked for -- so several multi-turn exchanges were only ever seen as their FIRST matching line (g3.r2.s1c, step45/L2145) rather than the full thread. It also did targeted `sed -n 'X,Yp'` range reads against the same export once it had located an interesting offset (step67 L3180-3222), which is how it caught the full v9-rewritten g3.r1.l1 exchange including konrad's rewritten 14:12 line. Mail was read thoroughly: both mail threads (g3.r1.l8, g3.r1.l12/g3.r2.s4d) were fetched and read as complete 4-5 message threads (12-22 line hits each), not just skimmed. Wiki was read via a page-fetch script (python3 /tmp/pw.py <page-id>) that pulls comments alongside the body -- both wiki-comment remarks (g3.r1.l5, g3.r2.s1a) were found early (steps 23 and 25), so BookStack's comment-indexing gap did not cost this run anything. Seven clues (g3.r2.say23, g3.r2.s2a, g3.r2.s4c, g3.r1.l7, g3.r2.s2d, g3.r1.l13, g3.r1.l9) were never surfaced at all -- all seven sit in #cookbooks/#code-review/#engineering/#general channel-days the regex sweeps happened not to dump in full; most of their content was independently recovered from other remarks or from the live source tree, except g3.r1.l13, whose 'TERMINAL zeroes the budget' rule had no other carrier.

A targeted sed range read at step 67 (transcript L3180-3222; full-JSON msg131 command `sed -n '9525,9550p' /tmp/chat.txt.n; echo '#####'; sed -n '2968,2990p' /tmp/chat.txt.n`) surfaces the entire #code-review exchange including konrad's new 14:12 line verbatim: 'and length does come good on a retry now and then, so dont stop retrying it, it just shouldnt get as many goes as a timeout' (transcript L3207). The agent shipped exactly the new meaning: `finish_reason was length` raises a ValueError, which classify_failure's type-based signal (2) maps to CONTRACT, and CONTRACT costs 2 attempts (_ATTEMPT_COSTS[CONTRACT]=2) but is still retried while budget allows (should_retry=remaining>=0) -- a contract, charged-2-and-retried treatment, not made terminal/non-retryable. g3.r1.rule scored 1, confirming this was graded correct. (transcript L3204-3209, L4818-4820 CONTRACT cost table, msg193 classify_failure ValueError->CONTRACT mapping)

The two facts most damaged (r1.exclusions_or_crossover, r1.observability) share one root cause: the TERMINAL-must-zero-the-budget rule's sole carrier (g3.r1.l13) was never surfaced, and the agent filled the gap by misapplying a DIFFERENT, correctly-found remark (g3.r2.say20, about the TRACKER's counters) to the REQUEST's attempts_left field, further reinforced by a genuine misreading of mail g3.r1.l8 (transcript L2772: 'MSG 114 mentions auth failures shouldnt consume remaining attempts (TERMINAL abort -- consistent)' -- that mail is entirely about THROTTLE/waivers and never once mentions TERMINAL or auth failures). This is a task-authoring-adjacent finding worth flagging: the agent's own reasoning shows how easy it is to conflate 'nothing else on the tracker moves' (r2.scope) with 'nothing about the request's own budget moves either' (r1.exclusions) when the carrier for the latter is missing.

g3.r2.rule failed for an unrelated, narrower reason: the agent's remaining_cooldown_seconds implementation clamps at zero but never rounds to three decimals, because the only remark carrying that instruction (g3.r2.s1c) was seen only as its opening line via a regex hit (transcript L2147) -- the reply containing 'clamp at 0.0, round to three decimals' was never dumped. The monotonic-max and field-placement halves of the same requirement (carried by 8 other remarks) were all shipped correctly and pass their assertions in the same test function.

All four herrings (g3.r1.h1/h2, g3.r2.h1/h2) were correctly identified as reversed and NOT followed in the shipped code -- the waiver-pool-of-6 design and the max()-floor cooldown design both match the reversals, not the original (wrong) decisions.
